memory: I oversee multi-state bridge coating projects and began a winter hybrid schedule in October 2024, working at Pittsburgh HQ Tuesday through Thursday and remotely Monday and Friday.
I attend weekly Tuesday briefings in the HQ boardroom at 2:00 PM as of October 1, 2024, after moving them from the bridge site.
I drive from Upper St. Clair, PA to 1 PPG Place, Pittsburgh for work.
I use SAP ERP to review project budgets and reconcile material cost allocations.
I use CorrosionCalc to simulate degradation rates for the Monongahela bridge project.
I use Microsoft Project for bridge coating timelines and resource leveling, including a 12% mobilization buffer for Monongahela and Liberty Bridge work.
I track Tank Lining Field Repairs - Unit 4 as Project ID PRJ-TL-2023-084, SAP cost center 4402-B, and internal tracking ID 992834-XP.
I oversaw the 31st Street Bridge (William Raymond Prom Memorial Bridge) Phase II overcoat project, covering approximately 42,000 sq ft, with final Q4 reporting completed in December 2024.
My 31st Street Bridge Phase II specifications use SSPC-SP 10 for primary girders and SSPC-SP 11 for pedestrian railings and floor system connections.
My 31st Street Bridge Phase II coating schedule uses zinc-rich MCU primer at 3-5 mils, high-build MCU intermediate at 5-7 mils, and semi-gloss MCU finish at 3 mils.
My 31st Street Bridge project uses Prom Memorial Blue for pedestrian railings and Federal Standard No. 16187 Gray for main spans.
I hold a Friday 1:30 PM close-out review of bridge project status, family finances, and physical fatigue to protect weekend family time.
I keep industrial project VOC compliance records in Notion and cross-reference coating technical data sheets against procurement logs.
I use AutoCAD LT to generate coating specification redlines, including Refinery Shutdown Unit 7, Project RFN-2024-02.
I protect a biweekly Wednesday morning hour for strategic planning of my Wexford senior advisory transition.
I use the Tru-Inspection mobile app on a tablet for dry film thickness logging under PPG's digitization mandate, including low-reception lower-deck bridge inspections.
I completed the 31st Street Bridge Phase II coating contract in May 2024 at 3.8% under budget with no recordable safety incidents.
I work roughly 60-hour weeks during the Wexford advisory transition and summer construction surge.
I suspended my weekly industry news review during the high workload of the Wexford transition.

My Ohio River Bridge Restoration project is ORB-2024-REST, with a three-coat system of organic zinc-rich epoxy primer at 3-5 mils, high-build polyamide epoxy intermediate at 8-10 mils, and aliphatic polyurethane topcoat at 2-3 mils.
I completed the Q2 maintenance audit and subsequent documentation close-out for the 16th Street Bridge (David McCullough Bridge) in August 2024.
I maintain a 6:30 PM work cutoff to protect evening family time.

I completed the Q4 Monongahela structural coating project with a 9.5 mil intermediate DFT target and 2.7 mil final topcoat; PennDOT accepted it after the November 28, 2024 walkthrough, and I archived it in December.
I prefer in-person mentoring over written documentation for transferring complex professional knowledge.
I reserve Mondays from 7:30 to 8:15 AM for my 2025 project pipeline review in Notion, including Fort Pitt Bridge Subdeck Phase I, Monongahela Transit Corridor, and Wexford North Extension Phase IV.
I am preparing a January 6, 2025 bridge infrastructure mobilization with a specialized crew starting at 7:00 AM on a 10/4 rotation.
